q-afrikanische-reiche-49#choices.1: An Arab merchant dynasty from Oman
q-afrikanische-reiche-49#choices.2: A ruler's title in the Mutapa Empire
q-afrikanische-reiche-49#explanation: Swahili culture grew from African roots in exchange with Arab, Persian and Indian merchants; today Swahili is one of the most widely spoken languages in Africa.
q-afrikanische-reiche-50#question: In what order did the great West African empires succeed one another?
q-afrikanische-reiche-50#explanation: Ghana was followed by Mali, founded by Sundiata around 1235; Songhai rose to become a great power under Sunni Ali in the 15th century.
q-afrikanische-reiche-51#question: What does the title Mansa mean?
q-afrikanische-reiche-51#choices.1: A caravan leader in the Sahara
q-afrikanische-reiche-51#choices.2: A scholarly rank at the Sankore Mosque
q-afrikanische-reiche-51#choices.3: Ruler or king in the Mali Empire
q-afrikanische-reiche-51#explanation: Mansa is a Malinke word for king or emperor; the Mansa stood at the head of a network of provinces and tributary princes.
q-afrikanische-reiche-52#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-afrikanische-reiche-52#choices.0: The rock-hewn churches of Lalibela are created
q-afrikanische-reiche-52#choices.1: The king of Kongo is baptized
q-afrikanische-reiche-52#explanation: Ezana converted to Christianity around 330; Lalibela followed around 1200, the baptism in Kongo in 1491 and Shaka's rise in 1816.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-01#question: Which culture is regarded as the "mother culture" of Mesoamerica?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-01#explanation: From about 1200 BC the Olmecs created the first centers of Mesoamerica on the Gulf coast and shaped later cultures.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-02#question: What was the name of the Aztec capital that lay on islands in Lake Texcoco?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-02#explanation: The Mexica founded Tenochtitlan in 1325; Mexico City stands on its site today.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-03#question: What were quipus used for in the Inca empire?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-03#choices.2: For recording numbers and information with knots
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-03#explanation: Quipus were knotted cords with which officials recorded inhabitants, levies and stores.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-04#question: In which present-day country is the Inca site of Machu Picchu located?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-04#explanation: Machu Picchu lies in the Andes of Peru above the Urubamba Valley, not far from Cusco.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-05#question: Which three cities formed the Aztec Triple Alliance in 1428?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-05#explanation: After the victory over the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco, Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan joined forces.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-06#question: Which Maya city did King Pakal rule from 615 to 683?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-06#explanation: Pakal had the Temple of the Inscriptions built at Palenque, where his tomb was found in 1952.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-07#question: Which settlement on the Mississippi, with Monks Mound, was the largest north of Mexico around 1100?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-07#explanation: Cahokia in present-day Illinois was the center of the Mississippian culture and probably had 10,000 to 20,000 inhabitants.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-08#question: Which culture laid out huge lines and animal figures in the desert of southern Peru?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-08#explanation: The Nazca created the geoglyphs by removing dark stones and exposing the light ground beneath.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-09#question: What does the confederacy of the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca call itself?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-09#explanation: Haudenosaunee means "people of the longhouse"; Europeans called the confederacy the Iroquois.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-10#question: From which great city came the influence that led to a change of dynasty at Tikal in 378?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-10#explanation: With the arrival of Siyaj K'ahk', a line of rulers connected with Teotihuacan came to power at Tikal.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-11#question: What was the name of the adobe-built capital of the Chimú kingdom?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-11#explanation: Chan Chan near Trujillo was the largest adobe city in the Americas until the Inca conquered the kingdom around 1470.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-12#question: Which Mesoamerican system of reckoning time counts the days since a starting date in 3114 BC?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-12#explanation: The Long Count allowed exact dates over centuries; the Tzolk'in and the Haab', by contrast, are recurring cycles.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-13#question: Which crop was domesticated in Mexico and became the staple food of Mesoamerica?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-13#explanation: Maize was bred from a wild grass in Mexico and grown together with beans and squash. The potato, by contrast, comes from the Andes.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-14#question: What were the artificial raised fields in the shallow lakes around Tenochtitlan called?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-14#explanation: Chinampas were beds of mud and plant matter bordered by canals that allowed several harvests a year. They are still farmed in Xochimilco today.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-15#question: What did the archaeologist Alberto Ruz Lhuillier discover in the Temple of the Inscriptions at Palenque in 1952?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-15#choices.0: A library of hundreds of Maya books
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-15#choices.1: The tomb of King Pakal with a jade death mask
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-15#choices.2: The oldest Long Count calendar stone
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-15#choices.3: Murals with the earliest Maya writing
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-15#explanation: Deep inside the pyramid lay Pakal's sarcophagus with a richly carved lid and a jade mask. The lid shows the king passing into the underworld.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-16#question: Which animals did the peoples of the Andes keep as pack and wool animals?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-16#explanation: Llamas carried loads in caravans, while alpacas provided fine wool. Horses, cattle and sheep only reached the Americas with the Europeans.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-17#question: What title, meaning “he who speaks” in Nahuatl, did the rulers of the city-states of central Mexico hold?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-17#explanation: The tlatoani of Tenochtitlan was chosen by a council of the ruling family and served as commander, judge and mediator with the gods. As huey tlatoani, great speaker, he stood above the other rulers.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-18#question: What role did Lady Six Sky play in the Maya city of Naranjo from 682 onwards?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-18#choices.0: She led a coup as a general from Teotihuacan
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-18#choices.1: She renewed the dynasty and governed the city for her young son
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-18#choices.2: She presided as a priestess over offerings at the sacred cenote
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-18#choices.3: As Pakal's wife she had the Temple of the Inscriptions built
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-18#explanation: The princess from Dos Pilas came to Naranjo to revive its weakened royal house; her son became king in 693 at the age of five. Stelae show her standing over captives like a king.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-19#question: What are the Olmecs of Mexico's Gulf Coast especially famous for?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-19#choices.0: Colossal basalt heads weighing many tons
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-19#choices.1: Huge lines and figures drawn in the desert
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-19#choices.2: A capital city built of mud brick
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-19#choices.3: A road network with suspension bridges
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-19#explanation: At centres such as San Lorenzo and La Venta the Olmecs carved massive stone heads, probably portraits of their rulers. As Mesoamerica's oldest civilisation they influenced the Maya and the Aztecs.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-20#question: What is an ayllu in the Andes?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-20#choices.0: A rest station with storehouses on the Inca road
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-20#choices.1: A specialist who read the knotted cords
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-20#choices.2: A kinship and village community holding land in common
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-20#choices.3: A temple to the sun god in Cusco
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-20#explanation: Members of an ayllu traced themselves to a common ancestor, shared out the land and helped one another with work. In the Inca Empire the ayllu was the basic unit for tribute and labour service.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-21#question: To which culture did the tattooed Lady of Cao belong, whose tomb with crowns and war clubs was discovered in 2005?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-21#explanation: The mummy from the Huaca Cao Viejo pyramid on Peru's north coast dates from the 4th or 5th century. Her grave goods show that women in Moche society could hold the highest offices.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-22#question: What does the eagle on a cactus in the flag of Mexico commemorate?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-22#choices.0: The Aztec victory over the Tepanecs
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-22#choices.1: The arrival of the Spaniards under Cortés
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-22#choices.2: The founding of Tenochtitlan by the Mexica
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-22#choices.3: The building of the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-22#explanation: According to tradition, in 1325 the Mexica settled where they saw an eagle on a cactus, as their god Huitzilopochtli had foretold. Mexico City grew up on the ruins of Tenochtitlan.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-23#question: Which two sons of Huayna Capac fought a civil war for the Inca throne after his death?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-23#explanation: Huáscar was recognised in Cusco, while Atahualpa relied on the seasoned army in the north. In 1532 Atahualpa's generals captured Huáscar shortly before Pizarro arrived.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-24#question: Which empire, with its capital near Ayacucho and administrative centres such as Pikillacta, is seen as a forerunner of Inca administration?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-24#explanation: Between about 600 and 1000 the Wari ruled much of Peru, built roads and already used knotted cords for record-keeping. Their art shares motifs such as the Staff God with Tiwanaku.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-25#question: What did the Inca ruler Huayna Capac probably die of around 1527?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-25#choices.1: An attack by his son Atahualpa
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-25#choices.3: Smallpox brought in by the Europeans
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-25#explanation: The disease spread from the European settlements faster than the Spaniards themselves. Because his designated heir also died, a civil war broke out that weakened the empire.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-26#question: From the language of which people do the words canoe, hammock, hurricane and tobacco come?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-26#explanation: The Taíno lived on the Greater Antilles in chiefdoms led by caciques, some of whom were women. Columbus met them on his very first voyage in 1492.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-27#question: Which Inca, while still serving as his father's general, subdued the kingdom of the Chimú around 1470?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-27#explanation: Túpac Yupanqui probably threatened the water supply of the coastal valleys and brought the Chimú king and many goldsmiths to Cusco. This gave the Incas control of the entire Peruvian coast.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-28#question: In which Maya city does the Pyramid of Kukulcan stand, where a shadow like a serpent's body appears at the equinoxes?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-28#explanation: Chichén Itzá in northern Yucatán rose to dominance after the collapse of the southern Maya cities. It also has the largest ball court in Mesoamerica.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-29#question: What is a cenote, such as the sacred cenote of Chichén Itzá?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-29#choices.0: A natural well in the limestone
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-29#choices.3: A burial chamber inside a pyramid
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-29#explanation: In Yucatán, which has hardly any rivers, these sinkholes were the most important sources of water. Offerings of gold and jade, and also people, were thrown into the sacred cenote.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-30#question: Which Maya city, with the enormous La Danta temple complex, flourished even before the birth of Christ?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-30#explanation: El Mirador in northern Guatemala was linked to neighbouring cities by raised causeways, the sacbeob. Around AD 150 it lost its importance to Tikal and Calakmul.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-31#question: What was the heavy rubber ball in the Mesoamerican ballgame usually played with?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-31#explanation: The ballgame was played across Mesoamerica for over 3,000 years on long courts enclosed by walls. It was a sport, a religious ritual and sometimes part of political ceremonies.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-32#question: Teotihuacan controlled the quarrying of which stone, used to make sharp blades and tools?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-32#explanation: Obsidian is volcanic glass that can be knapped into razor-sharp blades. Trade in it helped Teotihuacan influence art and politics as far away as Guatemala.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-33#question: Who made a decisive contribution to deciphering Maya writing in the 20th century?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-33#explanation: The Russian scholar Knorozov recognised that Maya glyphs include syllabic signs; Tatiana Proskouriakoff showed that the inscriptions record the history of rulers. Champollion, by contrast, deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-34#question: Near which lake did Tiwanaku, the religious centre of the southern Andes, lie?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-34#explanation: Tiwanaku lay at almost 4,000 metres in present-day Bolivia and is famous for its Gateway of the Sun. For the Incas, Lake Titicaca remained a sacred place of origin.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-35#question: Which people did the Aztecs later glorify as the inventors of all arts and as model ancestors?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-35#explanation: The Toltecs ruled from Tula until the city was destroyed or abandoned around 1150. The Aztecs derived the dignity of their own rulers from them.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-36#question: Which of these Andean cultures is the oldest?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-36#explanation: Chavín de Huántar became a pilgrimage centre from about 900 BC; its style is regarded as the first shared culture of the Andes. The Moche only flourished from about AD 100, the Wari from about 600 and the Chimú from the 10th century.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-37#question: Which great city in the Valley of Mexico had the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-37#explanation: The pyramids stand on an avenue several kilometres long that the Aztecs later called the Avenue of the Dead. Around AD 500 Teotihuacan was one of the largest cities in the world.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-38#question: Which people founded the city of Monte Albán around 500 BC on a levelled mountaintop above the Valley of Oaxaca?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-38#explanation: Monte Albán remained a centre of power for over a thousand years. Its early inscriptions are among the oldest written records in Mesoamerica.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-39#question: Which city was the capital of the Inca Empire?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-39#explanation: According to tradition, Pachacuti had Cusco rebuilt in the shape of a puma with the Coricancha sun temple. Lima, by contrast, was only founded by the Spaniards in 1535.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-40#question: What kinds of signs made up the Maya script?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-40#explanation: With word and syllable signs, Maya script could render anything that could be said in the language. Finds from San Bartolo show that the Maya were already writing in the 3rd century BC.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-41#question: What is terra preta in the Amazon region?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-41#choices.0: A network of causeways through the swamps
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-41#choices.1: A type of pottery with painted faces
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-41#choices.2: A sacred earth mound for burials
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-41#choices.3: Fertile dark earth created by humans
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-41#explanation: The dark soil formed from charcoal, refuse and manure of ancient settlements and is still fertile today. Like the mounds of the Marajoara culture, it shows that Amazonia was no untouched wilderness.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-42#question: What is considered a main cause of the collapse of the Classic Maya cities in the 9th century?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-42#choices.3: A volcanic eruption in the Valley of Mexico
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-42#explanation: Constant warfare and a loss of faith in the divine kings added to this; the last Long Count date comes from 909. The Maya did not vanish: cities in northern Yucatán continued to flourish.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-43#choices.2: Pachacuti's building of the Inca Empire
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-43#choices.3: The Inca conquest of the Chimú kingdom
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-43#explanation: According to tradition, Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325. The Triple Alliance followed in 1428, Pachacuti's seizure of power around 1438 and the conquest of Chimor around 1470.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-44#question: What is the Paracas culture on Peru's south coast especially famous for?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-44#choices.1: A Gateway of the Sun with a staff deity
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-44#choices.2: Mummy bundles wrapped in richly embroidered mantles
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-44#choices.3: Multi-storey great houses in a canyon
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-44#explanation: In the dry desert climate the textiles in the graves survived exceptionally well; Julio C. Tello discovered them in the 1920s. The Nazca culture later grew out of Paracas.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-45#question: Which deity was at the centre of the Inca state cult?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-45#explanation: Pachacuti made the sun cult the state religion, and the Inca ruler was regarded as the son of the sun. The Coricancha in Cusco was the most important sun temple.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-46#question: What is remarkable about the builders of the great earthworks of Poverty Point in Louisiana?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-46#choices.0: They were immigrants from the Olmec realm
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-46#choices.1: They used horses to move the earth
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-46#choices.2: They were hunters, fishers and gatherers, not farmers
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-46#choices.3: They left behind their own picture writing
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-46#explanation: Between about 1600 and 1100 BC they built six semicircular ridges without practising agriculture. Raw materials from hundreds of kilometres away show the site was a meeting place for trade and ceremonies.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-47#question: To which people did the Mexica of Tenochtitlan have to pay tribute until 1428?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-47#explanation: In 1428 Itzcoatl, together with Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco and the city of Tlacopan, defeated the Tepanecs. The Aztec Triple Alliance grew out of this victory.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-48#question: In which year was the Inca Atahualpa captured by the Spaniards under Francisco Pizarro?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-48#explanation: Atahualpa had just won the civil war against Huáscar when Pizarro seized him at Cajamarca. His capture ended the era of the independent Inca Empire.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-49#question: Who chose the members of the common council in the Haudenosaunee Confederacy and could also remove them?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-49#explanation: The women of the clans held great political influence in the confederacy. The council at Onondaga made its decisions by consensus under the Great Law of Peace.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-50#question: Who were the pochteca in the Aztec Empire?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-50#choices.1: Long-distance merchants who also served as scouts
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-50#choices.2: Warriors of the eagle and jaguar orders
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-50#choices.3: Scribes who drew up tribute lists
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-50#explanation: The pochteca brought luxury goods such as feathers, cacao and jade from distant regions to Tenochtitlan. Rulers like Ahuitzotl supported them because they brought back news of foreign lands.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-51#question: What is Nezahualcoyotl, ruler of Texcoco, still known for today?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-51#choices.0: As a poet-king to whom poems in Nahuatl are attributed
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-51#choices.1: As the last ruler of Tenochtitlan before the Spaniards
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-51#choices.2: As the founder of the city of Teotihuacan
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-51#choices.3: As the inventor of the Mesoamerican Long Count
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-51#explanation: Nezahualcoyotl supported scholars and artists and had a long dike built that protected Tenochtitlan from flooding. In 1428 he was a co-founder of the Aztec Triple Alliance.
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-52#question: How many days did the Mesoamerican ritual calendar comprise?
q-amerika-vorkolumbisch-52#explanation: The 260-day ritual calendar combined 20 day signs with the numbers 1 to 13. Together with the 365-day solar year it formed a cycle of 52 years.
q-antike-griechenland-01#question: In which city did the first democracy emerge in the 6th and 5th centuries BC?
q-antike-griechenland-01#explanation: In Athens the reforms of Cleisthenes laid the foundation of popular rule in 508 BC.
q-antike-griechenland-02#question: Where were the first recorded Olympic Games held in 776 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-02#explanation: The games were held every four years at Olympia in the Peloponnese in honor of Zeus.
q-antike-griechenland-03#question: Which battle decided the second Persian War at sea in 480 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-03#explanation: Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into the narrow bay of Salamis, where the Greek triremes prevailed.
q-antike-griechenland-04#question: Who won the Peloponnesian War, which ended in 404 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-04#explanation: With Persian money Sparta built a fleet and forced Athens to surrender in 404 BC.
q-antike-griechenland-05#question: Which philosopher was the teacher of Alexander the Great?
q-antike-griechenland-05#explanation: Aristotle taught the young Alexander at the Macedonian court before founding the Lyceum in Athens.
q-antike-griechenland-06#question: Which event is regarded as the end of the Hellenistic age?
q-antike-griechenland-06#choices.0: The destruction of Corinth in 146 BC
q-antike-griechenland-06#choices.1: The death of Cleopatra and the annexation of Egypt in 30 BC
q-antike-griechenland-06#choices.2: The death of Alexander in 323 BC
q-antike-griechenland-06#choices.3: The Battle of Pydna in 168 BC
q-antike-griechenland-06#explanation: With the suicide of Cleopatra VII, Egypt, the last Hellenistic kingdom, passed to Rome.
q-antike-griechenland-07#question: Which reform did Solon carry out in Athens around 594 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-07#choices.1: He gave women the right to vote
q-antike-griechenland-07#explanation: Solon cancelled debts and forbade the enslavement of citizens for debt; he divided the citizens into four classes according to wealth.
q-antike-griechenland-08#question: Who led the 300 Spartans at Thermopylae in 480 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-08#explanation: King Leonidas held the pass against the army of Xerxes with his Spartans and allies until every one of them had fallen.
q-antike-griechenland-09#question: Which poet from the island of Lesbos did Plato call the tenth Muse?
q-antike-griechenland-09#explanation: Around 600 BC Sappho wrote songs about love and longing; only fragments of her nine books survive.
q-antike-griechenland-10#question: Which temple was built on the Acropolis under Pericles between 447 and 432 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-10#explanation: The Parthenon, built by the architects Ictinus and Callicrates, was dedicated to the goddess Athena and housed a twelve-meter statue by Phidias.
q-antike-griechenland-11#question: What were Alexander's generals called, who fought over his empire after his death?
q-antike-griechenland-11#explanation: The Diadochi, the successors, waged war from 322 to 281 BC; in the end came the empires of the Ptolemies, the Seleucids and the Antigonids.
q-antike-griechenland-12#question: Which scholar was killed in 212 BC during the Roman capture of Syracuse?
q-antike-griechenland-12#explanation: Archimedes had supported the defense of his home city with war machines; a Roman soldier killed him against the orders of Marcellus.
q-antike-griechenland-13#question: What is the term for a Greek city-state made up of a city, its surrounding land and a self-governing community of citizens?
q-antike-griechenland-13#explanation: There were hundreds of poleis, from Athens and Sparta to small island towns, and their rivalry shaped Greek history. The word politics derives from polis.
q-antike-griechenland-14#question: According to legend, what did Archimedes celebrate with the cry “Eureka”?
q-antike-griechenland-14#choices.0: Calculating the circumference of the Earth
q-antike-griechenland-14#choices.1: Proving that there are infinitely many primes
q-antike-griechenland-14#explanation: Legend has it that the idea came to him in the bath when he noticed the displaced water. Archimedes also formulated the law of the lever and calculated pi with great accuracy.
q-antike-griechenland-15#question: Which Persian Great King sent the army that was defeated at Marathon in 490 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-15#explanation: Darius I wanted to punish Athens for supporting the Ionian Revolt. Ten years later his son Xerxes marched against Greece once again.
q-antike-griechenland-16#question: What purpose did the agora serve in a Greek city?
q-antike-griechenland-16#choices.0: It was the fortified upper city with the temples
q-antike-griechenland-16#choices.1: It was the training ground for the hoplites
q-antike-griechenland-16#choices.2: It was the theatre for the tragedies
q-antike-griechenland-16#choices.3: It was a marketplace, meeting place and political centre
q-antike-griechenland-16#explanation: In Athens the council house, law courts, colonnades and altars stood around the agora, and laws were publicly displayed there. It was also where Socrates held his conversations.
q-antike-griechenland-17#question: How many kings stood at the head of Sparta at the same time?
q-antike-griechenland-17#explanation: Sparta always had two kings from two different families, whose main task was to lead the army. The five ephors elected each year were overseers, not kings.
q-antike-griechenland-18#question: What legal status did Aspasia, the partner of Pericles, have in Athens?
q-antike-griechenland-18#choices.0: She was the daughter of an Athenian noble family
q-antike-griechenland-18#choices.1: She was a metic, a foreigner without citizenship
q-antike-griechenland-18#choices.2: She was a priestess of Athena on the Acropolis
q-antike-griechenland-18#choices.3: She was a freed slave from Thrace
q-antike-griechenland-18#explanation: Aspasia came from Miletus in Asia Minor; her son with Pericles received citizenship only as an exception. Her house was a meeting place for philosophers and artists.
q-antike-griechenland-19#question: Which epics are attributed to the poet Homer?
q-antike-griechenland-19#choices.2: The Theogony and Works and Days
q-antike-griechenland-19#explanation: The Iliad tells of the Trojan War, the Odyssey of the wanderings of Odysseus. Both epics were the foundation of Greek education.
q-antike-griechenland-20#question: Which Athenian divided the citizens into ten new tribes in 508/507 BC, laying the foundation of democracy?
q-antike-griechenland-20#explanation: The new tribes mixed city, coast and inland areas and so broke the power of the old noble families. A new Council of 500, with 50 members from each tribe, prepared the decisions of the assembly.
q-antike-griechenland-21#question: Which Athenian venture in the Peloponnesian War ended in disaster in 413 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-21#explanation: Athens sought to subdue Syracuse with a great fleet, but almost the entire army and fleet were lost. Athenian sea power never fully recovered from this blow.
q-antike-griechenland-22#question: Which event gave the marathon race its name?
q-antike-griechenland-22#choices.0: A race at the first Olympic Games
q-antike-griechenland-22#choices.2: The Athenian victory over the Persians in 490 BC
q-antike-griechenland-22#explanation: According to legend, a messenger ran from the battlefield at Marathon to Athens to announce the victory. The Athenians under Miltiades had charged the Persians at a run.
q-antike-griechenland-23#question: Why did Pericles introduce daily pay for officials and jurors?
q-antike-griechenland-23#choices.0: To recruit mercenaries for the war against Sparta
q-antike-griechenland-23#choices.1: So that poorer citizens could also take part in offices and courts
q-antike-griechenland-23#choices.2: To pay the builders on the Acropolis
q-antike-griechenland-23#choices.3: So that women and metics could also have a say
q-antike-griechenland-23#explanation: Without compensation only the wealthy could have afforded to serve the polis. Pericles was elected general again and again over several decades.
q-antike-griechenland-24#question: Which drama by Aeschylus, from 472 BC, is considered the oldest surviving drama in world literature?
q-antike-griechenland-24#explanation: The Persians shows the Battle of Salamis from the point of view of the defeated. Aeschylus introduced the second actor and thus made dialogue possible.
q-antike-griechenland-25#question: How was the death sentence against Socrates carried out in 399 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-25#choices.0: He was thrown from a cliff
q-antike-griechenland-25#choices.2: He was beheaded with a sword
q-antike-griechenland-25#choices.3: He drank a cup of hemlock poison
q-antike-griechenland-25#explanation: Socrates had been charged with not recognising the city's gods and corrupting the young. He refused to flee because he respected the laws of Athens.
q-antike-griechenland-26#question: Which Athenian commander lured the Persian fleet into the narrow strait of Salamis in 480 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-26#explanation: In the narrows the agile Greek triremes were able to defeat Xerxes' superior numbers. Themistocles had earlier persuaded Athens to build a large fleet.
q-antike-griechenland-27#question: Whose money did Sparta use to build the fleet that forced Athens to surrender in 404 BC?
q-antike-griechenland-27#explanation: Sparta, a land power, could only defeat Athenian sea power with Persian backing. The war was described by the contemporary historian Thucydides.
q-antike-griechenland-28#question: Which ancient physician, through the oath named after him, is still regarded as the model of medical ethics?
q-antike-griechenland-28#explanation: Around 420 BC Hippocrates taught on the island of Kos that diseases have natural causes and are not sent by the gods. His principle was above all to do no harm.
q-antike-griechenland-29#explanation: Marathon was fought in 490 BC, Thermopylae in 480 and Plataea in 479 BC. Alexander the Great only defeated the Persians at Issus in 333 BC.
q-antike-griechenland-30#question: Which sculptor created the twelve-metre statue of Athena in gold and ivory inside the Parthenon?
q-antike-griechenland-30#explanation: Phidias belonged to Pericles' circle and directed the sculptural decoration of the Parthenon. He also made the statue of Zeus at Olympia, one of the Seven Wonders.
q-antike-griechenland-31#question: Who was the father of Alexander the Great?
q-antike-griechenland-31#explanation: Philip II made Macedon the leading power in Greece. After his assassination Alexander became king at the age of 20.
q-antike-griechenland-32#question: Which historian described the Peloponnesian War as a contemporary?
q-antike-griechenland-32#explanation: Thucydides was himself an Athenian general and set out to explain the causes of the war soberly. Herodotus, by contrast, had described the Persian Wars.
q-antike-griechenland-33#question: Which school did Aristotle found in Athens?
q-antike-griechenland-33#explanation: Aristotle had previously studied for twenty years at Plato's Academy. His writings on logic, biology, ethics and politics shaped scholarship into the Middle Ages.
q-antike-griechenland-34#question: Who is known as the “Father of History”?
q-antike-griechenland-34#explanation: Cicero gave Herodotus this title. In his Histories he set out to explain why Greeks and Persians went to war, describing many lands and peoples along the way.
q-antike-griechenland-35#question: What were the unfree rural people called who worked the fields for the citizens of Sparta?
q-antike-griechenland-35#explanation: Because the helots farmed the land, Spartan citizens could devote themselves entirely to military service. Fear of helot revolts shaped Sparta as a military state.
q-antike-griechenland-36#question: In which oasis did Alexander the Great have himself greeted by the oracle of Ammon as the son of the god?
q-antike-griechenland-36#explanation: Alexander visited the oasis in the Libyan Desert after the Egyptians had welcomed him as their liberator from the Persians. That same winter of 332/331 BC he founded the city of Alexandria on the coast.
q-antike-griechenland-37#question: Which god proclaimed his oracles at Delphi through the priestess Pythia?
q-antike-griechenland-37#explanation: Cities and kings consulted the oracle before founding colonies, waging wars and passing reforms. The temple bore the inscription “Know thyself”.
q-antike-griechenland-38#question: Which modern city goes back to the Greek colony of Massalia?
q-antike-griechenland-38#explanation: Massalia was founded around 600 BC by Greeks from Phocaea. Hundreds of Greek colonies arose from Spain to the Black Sea.
q-antike-griechenland-39#question: Which scholar in Alexandria calculated the circumference of the Earth with astonishing accuracy?
